subject: Data chain review — no customer data exposed
messages:
From: Elena Vega <security@nimbushealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Trevor Mills <trevor@pacificbank.com>
Date: 2027-05-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data chain review request - May 27

Hi Soojin,

We saw the notification earlier this morning about a transient routing issue that affected a small subset of hosted inference requests. Our security and privacy team is doing a quick impact assessment. For our audit records we need a concise statement confirming whether any Nimbus Health customer data was exposed or exfiltrated during the incident, and the supporting artefacts used to reach that conclusion. Specifically: 

- A confirmation (yes/no) on whether any customer PII or file payloads were accessed outside of normal processing flows.
- Hashes or checksums of relevant request logs to match against our ingestion records (we will share our side once we get yours).
- Any known cache/KV persistence that could have retained customer data beyond expected TTLs.

Can you share these items today? If you prefer, a short call later this afternoon with your incident owner would also work.

Thanks,
Elena Vega
Director, Security Operations
Nimbus Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Vega <security@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-27T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data chain review request - May 27

Elena — thanks for the clear checklist. Short answer up front: no customer data was exfiltrated and our chain-of-custody checks show no unauthorized access outside of our processing environment. Below are the items we are providing and the reasoning we used. Attached: audit_hashes_20270527.csv and forensic_summary_27may2027.pdf.

Summary findings (high level):
- No external transfer detected: network egress and object-store access logs show zero anomalous outbound connections during the incident window (05:43 - 05:49 UTC).
- Request log hash reconciliation: we generated SHA256 checksums over the canonicalized request log segments covering the affected shards. Those hashes are in audit_hashes_20270527.csv (column format: shard_id,start_ts,end_ts,sha256). You can reconcile these with your ingestion IDs.
- Ephemeral cache scan: we ran a TTL sweep and KV cache tombstone check. All ephemeral caches were cleared by the automated TTL job within expected bounds; no entries exceeded configured retention.
- No key compromise indicators: key usage patterns were normal and KMS audit events show no unusual access patterns.

Technical notes (for your engineers):
- The root cause was a misrouted internal control message that caused a handful of requests to be processed on a failover path with identical model weights but slightly different telemetry tagging. No payload rewriting or external replication occurred.
- We verified that all denylisted endpoints remained blocked and that rate limits prevented any batch-level leakage.

Next steps we propose:
1) We will publish the CSV checksums to a short-lived Drive folder and share the link (see JIRA entry below).
2) If you want additional evidence we can provide sanitized request ids and a short runbook of the hash generation process.

I copy Rishi and Monica who ran the hash generation and forensic collection. Grace from Customer Success is on copy for any compliance paperwork.

Best,
So — Soojin Lee
VP, Security & Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: [audit_hashes_20270527.csv] (csv, 12 KB), [forensic_summary_27may2027.pdf] (pdf, 420 KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Vega <security@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-27T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data chain review request - May 27

Elena / team — adding a little color on the generation process so you can validate independently: 

On Thu, May 27, 2027 at 11:20 AM Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the clear checklist. Short answer up front: no customer data was exfiltrated and our chain-of-custody checks show no unauthorized access outside of our processing environment. Below are the items we are providing and the reasoning we used. Attached: audit_hashes_20270527.csv and forensic_summary_27may2027.pdf.

Process details: 
- Canonicalization: we remove non-deterministic fields (request_id, processing_time_ms, ephemeral_token) then sort JSON keys deterministically before hashing. This ensures both sides can reproduce a byte-identical input for SHA256.
- Shard windowing: logs were sliced by shard and 1-minute boundaries (UTC) as detailed in the CSV. If you share three sample request_ids from your side we can point to the exact shard file and byte offsets.
- Forensic summary: the PDF includes the signed manifest (redwood-kms:KEY-197) of the exported shard files and a brief timeline of host-level checks.

If you'd like, we can open a secure SFTP session for you to pull the shard files directly; we can rotate credentials per your preference.

-Rishi
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Vega <security@nimbushealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Trevor Mills <trevor@pacificbank.com>
Date: 2027-05-28T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data chain review request - May 27

Soojin / Rishi — thank you, that level of detail is exactly what we needed. We reconciled the hashes against our ingestion records for the sample window and they match. Nimbus Security accepts the conclusion that there was no exposure of customer PII.

Two quick asks to close our audit ticket: 
1) Can you upload the signed manifest (referenced in the forensic PDF) into our vendor portal or share a short-lived Drive link so our audit team has access?
2) Please confirm whether Redwood will log this as a P0 incident in your internal tracker and whether any formal postmortem will be published (we just need the postmortem URL or a short executive summary).

If both are OK, we'll mark this as closed on our end. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Elena
Elena Vega
Director, Security Operations
Nimbus Health
